_comment: Windows-native baseline app list, in the same spirit as macos/Brewfile. Entries here are installed by install-apps.ps1 and checked/wired up by bootstrap.ps1. ES-DE ships its own Windows es_systems.xml covering all of these out of the box (registry + PATH + Emulators\<dir>\ detection) -- there is no custom XML to render, unlike macos/ and the Linux distrobox tree.

apps.name: ES-DE
apps.notes: Frontend. Installer release puts its home directory at %USERPROFILE%\ES-DE (see windows/README.md).

apps.name: Dolphin
apps.notes: GameCube/Wii. ES-DE's find-rules only check PATH and %ESPATH%\Emulators\Dolphin-x64\Dolphin.exe -- no registry rule. bootstrap.ps1 -Action Configure creates that junction automatically if Dolphin.exe isn't already on PATH.

apps.name: PCSX2
apps.notes: PlayStation 2. PATH and %ESPATH%\Emulators\PCSX2-Qt\pcsx2-qt*.exe only -- no registry rule for the current Qt build.

apps.name: DuckStation
apps.notes: PlayStation 1. PATH and %ESPATH%\Emulators\duckstation\<exe> only -- no registry rule.

apps.name: PPSSPP
apps.notes: PSP. ES-DE reads InstallLocation from the PPSSPP_is1 uninstall key, so a normal installer-based winget install is usually auto-detected without a junction.

apps.name: RetroArch
systems: multi-system: nes, snes, genesis, gba, gbc, atari2600, and many more via cores
apps.notes: Cores are NOT installed by winget -- open RetroArch once after install and use Online Updater > Core Downloader for the systems you want (see windows/README.md). ES-DE checks the App Paths registry entry the RetroArch installer registers, so it's usually auto-detected.

future.name: RPCS3
future.notes: No winget package -- RPCS3 project policy is against third-party redistribution; download manually from rpcs3.net.

future.name: Eden
future.notes: Requires user-supplied decryption keys/firmware, same as upstream.
